attempts.plan:
1. Read both CSV files into pandas: one containing borough names and Waste values, and one containing the neighborhood‐pairs list.  
2. Identify and drop the single borough whose Waste_value is NaN.  
   • It will not be used in any calculations, and it cannot be reported as a hot or cold spot.  
   • If a dropped borough appears in a neighbor list, simply omit that missing neighbor from the local‐area sum of the remaining boroughs.  
3. For every remaining borough i, build the set Sᵢ = {i plus all of its listed neighbors that still have non-missing Waste_value}.  
4. For each borough i, compute the local aggregate Waste_i* = Σ Waste_value over Sᵢ.  
5. Calculate the citywide mean (μ) and sample standard deviation (σ) of all Waste_i* values.  
6. Compute a simple z-score for each borough: z_i = (Waste_i* – μ) / σ.  
   • This mimics a Gi* statistic but uses the “combined local sum” requirement instead of spatial weights.  
7. Classify significance:  
   • HOT spot if z_i > 2.576 (99%) or 1.96 < z_i ≤ 2.576 (95%).  
   • COLD spot if z_i < –2.576 (99%) or –2.576 ≤ z_i < –1.96 (95%).  
8. Collect every borough whose z_i meets either threshold; label it HOT or COLD and record the z-score twice as required (Gi*=…, gi_value=…).  
9. Count data_points_used = number of boroughs after removing the one with the missing value.  
10. Print:  
   • data_points_used = <integer>  
   • FINAL ANSWER line, f-string built from the list of significant borough strings (or “none” if none qualify).

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from collections import defaultdict

# Paths supplied in the prompt
WASTE_PATH = "chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_2022_waste.csv"
ADJ_PATH   = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

# 1. Read the data
waste_df = pd.read_csv(WASTE_PATH)
adj_df   = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)

# 2. Drop the single borough with a missing Waste_value
waste_df_clean = waste_df.dropna(subset=['Waste_value']).copy()
usable_boroughs = set(waste_df_clean['borough'])

# 3. Build undirected neighbor dictionary (only keep usable boroughs)
neighbors = defaultdict(set)
for _, row in adj_df.iterrows():
    b, n = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    if b in usable_boroughs and n in usable_boroughs:
        neighbors[b].add(n)
        neighbors[n].add(b)        # make the graph undirected

# 4. Compute local aggregate (borough + its neighbors)
local_sums = {}
for b in usable_boroughs:
    S_i = neighbors[b] | {b}                       # union with itself
    local_sums[b] = waste_df_clean.set_index('borough').loc[list(S_i), 'Waste_value'].sum()

# 5. Citywide mean and std of local sums
local_vals = np.array(list(local_sums.values()))
mu  = local_vals.mean()
sigma = local_vals.std(ddof=1)                     # sample std

# 6. Gi* (here simple z-score of the local sum distribution)
gi_scores = {b: (s - mu) / sigma for b, s in local_sums.items()}

# 7. Identify significant hot / cold spots (|z| > 1.96)
significant = {}
for b, z in gi_scores.items():
    if z > 1.96:
        significant[b] = ("HOT", z)
    elif z < -1.96:
        significant[b] = ("COLD", z)

# 8. Prepare the results line
results = [f"{b} ({label}, Gi*={z}, gi_value={z})" for b, (label, z) in significant.items()]

# 9. Count of data points actually used
data_points_used = len(usable_boroughs)

# 10. Print outputs in the required format
print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")
if results:
    print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {', '.join(results)}")
else:
    print("FINAL ANSWER: none")
